Mitchell invests \$600 000 for 8 years at $4.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.

Calculate the value of his investment after 8 years.

solutions.latex:
Using the compound interest formula:
$$\begin{aligned} FV&=PV(1+r)^n\\ &=600\,000(1+4.5\%)^8\\ &=\$853\,260.37\end{aligned}$$

parts.latex: The cost of the weekly groceries for the Stewart family in January 2016 was \$228.00. Since 2016, the inflation rate in Australia has averaged at $1.9\%$ p.a. If this rate continues, what will be the cost of their weekly groceries in January 2020?

solutions.latex:
There are 4 years from January 2016 to January 2020.
$$\begin{aligned} FV&=228.00\times(1+1.9\%)^4\\ &\approx\$245.83\end{aligned}$$
This matches option D.

parts.latex:
Peter invests \$26 000 in an account that pays $5.4\%$ p.a. interest, compounded quarterly.

Which calculation would give the value of the investment after 18 months?

solutions.latex:
18 months is 6 quarters.

The quarterly rate is $5.4\% \div 4 = 1.35\%$.
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 26000 \times (1 + 1.35\%)^6 \\ &= 26000 \times (1.0135)^6 \end{aligned}$$
Hence the answer is option D.

parts.latex: In July 2020, the inflation rate in a certain country was reported to be $4.1\%$ per day. If a chocolate bar costs \$2.50 today, what will its price be 90 days from now if its price increases in line with the inflation rate in that country?

solutions.latex:
Using the future value formula $FV = PV(1 + r)^n$:
$$\begin{aligned} FV &= 2.50(1 + 0.041)^{90} \\ &= 93.0048\ldots \\ &\approx \$93.00 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore \text{the chocolate bar costs } \$93.00 \text{ in 90 days}$$
criteria: Uses the future value formula with at least one correct value, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
\$4000 is invested at a rate of 6.3% p.a. compounded monthly for 3 years.

Find the amount in the account at the end of the 3 years.

solutions.latex:
Use the compound interest formula $A = P\left(1+r\right)^n$, with monthly rate and number of months:
$$\begin{aligned} P &= 4000 \\ r &= \dfrac{0.063}{12} \\ n &= 3\times 12 = 36 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} A &= 4000\left(1+\dfrac{0.063}{12}\right)^{36} \\ &\approx 4829.78 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{the amount is } \$4829.78$$
criteria: Substitutes $r=\dfrac{0.063}{12}$ and $n=36$ into the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit

Oskar and Jett both have \$3000 to invest for 5 years.

Oskar chooses to invest his money in bank (A) at 6.3% p.a. with interest compounded monthly. Jett prefers a simple interest option.

Calculate the yearly interest rate Jett will need to obtain from the bank to have the same amount in the account as Oskar at the end of the 5 years. Give your answer correct to two decimal places.

solutions.latex:
Oskar's amount uses the compound interest formula with $r=\dfrac{0.063}{12}$ per month and $n=5\times12=60$ months.
$$\begin{aligned} A&=3000\left(1+\dfrac{0.063}{12}\right)^{60}\\ &\approx \$4107.39 \end{aligned}$$
Interest earned is $4107.39-3000=\$1107.39$.

For Jett, use simple interest $I=Prn$ with $P=3000$ and $n=5$.
$$\begin{aligned} 1107.39&=3000\times r\times 5\\ r&=\dfrac{1107.39}{15\,000}\\ &\approx 0.0738 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Jett needs } 7.38\% \text{ p.a.}$$
criteria: Finds Oskar's interest and sets up the simple interest equation, or equivalent merit

Hazel is planning a month long vacation to Europe in $3$ years' time. She estimates she will need \$9 000 to pay for the trip. She plans to invest a single sum of money in an account paying $7.2\%$ per annum, compounding quarterly.

What single investment must Hazel make to reach her goal of \$9 000?

solutions.latex:
The quarterly rate is $\dfrac{7.2}{4}=1.8\%$, with $3\times 4=12$ quarters.
$$9000 = PV\left(1 + \dfrac{1.8}{100}\right)^{12}$$
$$\begin{aligned} PV &= \dfrac{9000}{\left(1 + \frac{1.8}{100}\right)^{12}} \\ &= \$7265.56 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Substitutes into the compound interest formula, or equivalent merit
